metaDescription: Six digital kitchen scales compared by capacity, power source, display and cleanup, for home cooks who want readable, repeatable measurements.
introParagraphs: A digital kitchen scale replaces guesswork with a number, and that number is worth having for baking, portion control and any recipe written in grams. The scales themselves look nearly identical in photos, though, so the differences that matter, such as capacity, power source and how easy the display is to read, are easy to overlook.

This lineup covers six digital models, from compact 11 pound units that run on two AAA batteries to rechargeable 33 pound scales with glass platforms. We evaluated them from product specs and buyer feedback, focusing on how each is powered, how clearly it shows weight, and how simple it is to wipe clean after flour and spills.

For most home cooks, 1 gram resolution is plenty. The better question is whether you want batteries, a charging cable, or a waterproof body. Also decide where the scale will live, because a drawer-sized model gets used far more often than a large one that has to be hauled out of a cabinet. Whichever you choose, set it on a hard, flat counter and zero it with the bowl in place before every recipe.

products.name: Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale

specList.label: Units
specList.value: oz, lb:oz, fl oz, g, mL

products.description:
This is the straightforward choice: a small, sleek scale that weighs up to 11 pounds (5 kg) in 1 gram steps. It supports five units, covering oz, lb:oz, fl oz, grams and milliliters, and a tare button lets you zero out the bowl.

Two AAA batteries come in the box, so it works as soon as you unwrap it. The compact design is meant to slide into a cabinet without eating counter space. The tradeoff is capacity and power: 11 pounds is plenty for recipes but limits bulk weighing, and batteries eventually need replacing.

It is the pick for someone who wants the basics done well. Compared with the Etekcity 22 lb Digital Food Scale with IPX6 Rating, it gives up capacity and waterproofing but is simpler and smaller, and next to the GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale it avoids the learning curve of touch controls.

cons: Capacity tops out at 11 lb for the whole load

products.name: Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale With LCD

specList.label: Units
specList.value: lb, oz, g, fl oz, ml

products.description:
The Amazon Basics scale pairs a stainless steel platform with a wide LCD screen and food-safe, BPA-free plastic components. It weighs up to 11 pounds, with a minimum reading of 2 grams and a top of about 5000 grams.

It shows results in pounds, ounces, grams, fluid ounces and milliliters, and includes a tare function. The stainless top is easy to wipe, and the wide display is easy to read at a glance. The tradeoff is the 2 gram minimum, which means very small amounts like a pinch of yeast will not register well.

It suits cooks who weigh bulk ingredients like flour, rice and meat rather than tiny quantities. In comparison with the Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale, which also tops out at 11 pounds, this one emphasizes the stainless platform and wide readout, while the Nicewell 22 lb Digital Kitchen Scale offers double the capacity.
products.bestFor: Cooks weighing larger ingredients who value a wide display.
pros: Wide LCD screen is easy to read
Stainless platform wipes clean quickly
Food-safe BPA-free plastic components
Five units including milliliters
cons: Uses batteries rather than a rechargeable cell

products.name: Nicewell 22 lb Digital Kitchen Scale
products.description:
Nicewell builds this scale around four high-precision load sensors that respond to 1 gram or 0.1 ounce changes as ingredients are added. It supports g, kg, lb:oz, oz, fl oz and ml, and the capacity is 22 pounds.

The 9 by 6.3 inch platform is big enough for a mixing bowl, and the large LCD is easy to read. The design uses tempered glass for strength with a stainless steel top surface that resists fingerprints and wipes clean. The tradeoff is size: a larger platform takes more room to store, and glass is a hard surface that can chip if you drop a pan on it.

It is a strong all-purpose pick for cooks who weigh heavier bowls. Compared with the Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale it has double the capacity, and next to the Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale it gives up some capacity while keeping a familiar button layout.
products.bestFor: Bakers and meal preppers who weigh heavy mixing bowls.
pros: Four sensors respond to 1 g changes
Platform is large enough for big bowls
Stainless top resists fingerprints
22 lb capacity covers bulk prep

products.name: Etekcity 22 lb Digital Food Scale With IPX6 Rating

specList.label: Range
specList.value: 2 g to 22 lb in 1 g steps

products.description:
This is the cleanest scale to live with. It combines a 22 pound (10 kg) capacity with a USB-C rechargeable battery and an IPX6 waterproof design, so you can wipe it down after a messy batch and measure liquids with less worry.

It reads from 2 grams up to 22 pounds in 1 gram increments, offers five units including milk and water, and ships with a USB-C cable. Going rechargeable removes the chore of buying AAA cells. The tradeoff is that the listing does not state battery life in hours, and IPX6 handles splashes and rinsing rather than full immersion.

It is the pick for cooks who hate cleaning around electronics. Where the Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale uses AAA cells and has a lower ceiling, this model is better sealed and rechargeable, and it has less capacity than the GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale.

products.name: GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale
products.description:
GGQ offers the highest capacity in this group at 33 pounds, with four high-precision load sensors and a glass weighing panel the listing calls anti-collision. A touch screen sits alongside a large LCD.

Five units cover grams, kilograms, pounds with ounces, ounces and milliliters, and the tare button subtracts the weight of a mug, plate or bowl. The smooth glass wipes clean quickly. The tradeoffs are practical: the listing gives no port type or battery hours, glass can chip if struck by a pan, and touch controls can be fussy with wet fingers.

It appeals to people who like a sleek, modern look and weigh bulk items. Against the Nicewell 22 lb Digital Kitchen Scale it offers more capacity and rechargeability, while the Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale matches its capacity but adds battery power as a backup.

products.name: Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale

specList.label: Units

products.description:
What sets the Deweywei apart is flexible power. It can charge over USB or run on two AAA batteries, so a dead rechargeable cell does not leave you without a scale on a busy baking day.

The capacity reaches 33 pounds, the measuring range starts at 0.1 ounce, and a unit button converts between five units: kilograms, grams, pounds with ounces, fluid ounces and milliliters. It is described as simple to use for both large and small projects. The tradeoff is that the listing gives little detail on materials, so cleanup and surface quality are less certain than on the glass or stainless models.

It makes the most sense as a backup-minded workhorse. Compared with the GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale it has the same capacity but a more traditional layout, and next to the Etekcity 22 lb Digital Food Scale with IPX6 Rating it offers more capacity but no stated waterproofing.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity is the maximum weight the scale can read, and it includes the container. A heavy ceramic mixing bowl can weigh several pounds before you add flour. The Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale and the Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale With LCD cover everyday recipes, while the Nicewell 22 lb Digital Kitchen Scale and GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale suit bulk prep. For most households, 11 to 22 pounds is plenty.

Resolution is the smallest increment the display shows, and for flour, butter and water, 1 gram is sufficient. The Amazon Basics scale lists a 2 gram minimum, so tiny additions like yeast may not register. If you measure small ingredients like salt or spices often, consider a separate scale with finer resolution. A fine display is useless if the platform is too heavy for the sensor to settle.

AAA models like the Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale are simple and ready out of the box, but cells need replacing. Rechargeable scales such as the Etekcity 22 lb Digital Food Scale With IPX6 Rating avoid that, yet they require remembering to charge. The Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale covers both with USB charging and AAA batteries. Pick the power style you will actually keep up with.

Stainless steel and tempered glass resist stains and wipe clean better than plain plastic. The Amazon Basics scale uses a stainless platform and the Nicewell 22 lb Digital Kitchen Scale pairs tempered glass with a steel top. An IPX6 rating, as on the Etekcity 22 lb model, lets you rinse the surface after a spill. Glass looks clean but can chip if you drop a pan on it.

A scale is only useful if you can read it with a bowl on top. A wide or extended display avoids the shadow cast by a large dish. The Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale With LCD advertises a wide LCD, and the Nicewell and GGQ models list large screens. Check that the digits are high contrast and that the screen is not hidden by a big platter.

Switching between grams and ounces should take one button press. Touch panels like the GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale look clean but can be fussy when your hands are wet, while the physical buttons on the Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale are easier to press with flour on your fingers. Tare must be fast too, since you will use it every time you add an ingredient.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated capacities from 11 to 33 pounds and minimum readings where listed. The GGQ 33 lb and Deweywei 33 lb models lead on capacity, while the Etekcity 11 lb and Amazon Basics scales cover everyday recipes. We did not reward capacity above what a home cook uses.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source
howWeEvaluated.description: Power affects convenience more than accuracy. We looked at batteries versus USB charging and dual options. The Deweywei 33 lb scale offers both, the Etekcity 22 lb model is USB-C rechargeable, and the 11 lb Etekcity uses AAA cells.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and build
howWeEvaluated.description: Surfaces and sealing were scored from listing details. The IPX6 design on the Etekcity 22 lb scale and the stainless platform on the Amazon Basics scale scored highest, with glass models rated for easy wiping but also for chip risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Display and controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the readability of each display and whether controls are physical or touch based. Large LCD screens earned points, and touch controls were noted as a possible issue with wet hands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Everyday usability
howWeEvaluated.description: Features like tare, unit switching and platform size shape daily use. The Nicewell 22 lb scale has the roomiest platform, and the Etekcity 11 lb scale the smallest footprint, so we positioned them as large-bowl and compact-storage leaders respectively.

faq.a: Most home cooks do well with 11 to 22 pounds. Remember that capacity includes the bowl, so a heavy ceramic one can use up a lot of it. The Etekcity 11 lb Digital Food Scale is enough for standard recipes, while the GGQ 33 lb Rechargeable Food Scale suits bulk prep.

Yes for flour, sugar, butter and liquids. It falls short for tiny ingredients like yeast or spices, where a 0.1 g scale helps. Note that the Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale With LCD lists a 2 gram minimum.

Tare zeroes the display after you place a bowl, so you weigh only the ingredient. Use it between each addition to build a recipe in one container. All six scales here include a tare function. A good habit is to tare, add one ingredient, tare again and add the next, so each amount is read directly and you never have to subtract anything in your head.

faq.q: Can I rinse a kitchen scale?
faq.a: Only if it is rated for it. An IPX6 rating, like the Etekcity 22 lb Digital Food Scale With IPX6 Rating, handles spray and rinsing but not full immersion. For the others, wipe with a damp cloth.
Tempered glass is strong but can chip if a heavy pan strikes an edge. The Nicewell and GGQ scales use glass, so set pans down gently. Stainless platforms avoid this risk.

faq.q: Why does my scale read differently each time?
faq.a: Common causes are a low battery, an uneven counter or a platform pressed against the wall. Place it on a flat surface and replace or recharge the power source. Let it settle before reading. Keep cords, towels and other objects clear of the platform edge, since anything touching the side of the scale can add or subtract a few grams without you noticing.

faq.q: Is a rechargeable scale better than a battery one?
faq.a: Neither is better outright. Rechargeable models like the Etekcity 22 lb scale save buying batteries but need charging, while AAA scales run until the cells die. The Deweywei 33 lb Digital Kitchen Scale avoids the choice by supporting both.
